cards: Emperor Wu was the seventh emperor of the Han Dynasty (r. 141–87 BCE).

Zhang Qian was a Han dynasty envoy sent west by Emperor Wu around 138 BCE to seek an alliance with the Yuezhi against the Xiongnu.
Gaius Marius was a Roman general and politician who held the consulship seven times.
Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman and writer of the second century BCE, famous for his conservatism and moral severity.
Aristonicus was a pretender to the throne of Pergamon who claimed to be a son of Eumenes II and took the royal name Eumenes III.
Masinissa was the first king of united Numidia.
Scipio Aemilianus was a Roman general and statesman who commanded the final siege of Carthage during the Third Punic War.
Attalus III was the last Attalid king of Pergamon, reigning from 138 BCE.
Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus was a Roman general who defeated King Perseus of Macedon at Pydna in 168 BCE, ending the Third Macedonian War and the Antigonid monarchy.
Antiochus IV Epiphanes was a Seleucid king who reigned from 175 to 164 BCE.
Quintus Ennius was a Latin poet, born in 239 BCE at Rudiae in the Messapian south of Italy.
Eumenes II was king of Pergamon in the early second century BCE and an ally of Rome.
Huo Qubing was a Han Dynasty general of the second century BCE, renowned for his cavalry campaigns against the Xiongnu under Emperor Wu.
Jugurtha was king of Numidia, a grandson of Masinissa who seized the whole kingdom after killing one adoptive brother and fighting the other.
Terence, in full Publius Terentius Afer, was a Roman comic playwright, said to have been born in North Africa and brought to Rome as a slave.
Palacus was a king of the Scythians in the Crimea in the late 2nd century BCE, a son of Scilurus.
Pharnaces I was king of Pontus from about 185 to about 160 BCE.
Titus Quinctius Flamininus was a Roman general and politician who defeated Philip V of Macedon at Cynoscephalae in 197 BCE, ending the Second Macedonian War.
Andriscus was a pretender who claimed to be Philip, son of Perseus, the last king of Macedon.
Bituitus was a king of the Arverni in Gaul in the late 2nd century BCE, son of Luernios.
Micipsa was king of Numidia from 148 to 118 BCE, the eldest legitimate son of Masinissa.
Pushyamitra Shunga was the founder of the Shunga dynasty of northern India.

Scilurus was a king of the Scythians in the Crimea in the 2nd century BCE, who ruled from Scythian Neapolis near modern Simferopol.
Skilurus was a king of the Scythians in the Crimea in the 2nd century BCE who ruled from Scythian Neapolis near modern Simferopol.
Viriathus was the leader of the Lusitanians in their war against Rome from about 147 to 139 BCE.
Ellalan, called Elara in the Pali chronicles, was a Tamil prince from the Chola country who ruled Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka for about 44 years in the 2nd century BCE.
r. c. 205–161 BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Gaius Gracchus was a Roman tribune of the plebs in 123 and 122 BCE who continued the reforms of his brother Tiberius.
Gulussa was a Numidian prince, a son of King Masinissa.
Mastanabal was a Numidian prince, one of the three legitimate sons of King Masinissa.
Tiberius Gracchus, in full Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, was a Roman tribune of the plebs in 133 BCE.
Dutugemunu was a Sinhalese king of the Anuradhapura Kingdom who reigned from about 161 to 137 BCE.
r. c. 161–137 BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Emperor Wen of Han, born Liu Heng, was a son of Liu Bang who was made King of Dai before being chosen emperor in 180 BCE after the fall of the Lü clan.
Nagasena was a Buddhist monk who, according to the Milindapanha, debated questions of doctrine with King Milinda, the Indo-Greek ruler Menander I, and won him over to Buddhism.
c. 2nd century BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Ptolemy Apion was a son of Ptolemy VIII who became king of Cyrene when Cyrenaica was separated from Egypt around 116 BCE.
Zariadres was a general of the Seleucid king Antiochus III, appointed governor of Sophene around 200 BCE while his colleague Artaxias received Greater Armenia.
Zhao Tuo was a Qin general sent to conquer the far south who founded the kingdom of Nanyue, with its capital at Panyu (Guangzhou), in 204 BCE.
Agnimitra was the second king of the Shunga dynasty of northern India, son of its founder Pushyamitra Shunga, in the 2nd century BCE.
Antialcidas was an Indo-Greek king who ruled from Taxila in the late 2nd century BCE.
r. c. 115–95 BCE · South & Southeast Asia
